industry_knowledge.evidence: Slide 5: "PUCKIPUPPY makes dog-breed-named ebikes - Labrador Pro (~$1,399), Boxer ST, Corgi, Husky trike" plus UL 2849/2271 certs and Slide 6: "California DTC brand est. 2022 by founder Bob, named for his dog Puck; ~145K monthly visits, 11-50 employees" - real company facts with dates and product specifics. However Slide 6's competitive read is "premium DTC vs value brands vs PUCKIPUPPY trust-led" with no named competitor anywhere in the deck.
industry_knowledge.fix: Name at least two real ebike competitors (e.g., Lectric, Aventon, Ride1Up, Rad Power) with a price/positioning data point on Slide 6 to satisfy the 'competitor or category position' bar for a 5.

business_opportunity.evidence: Slide 4: "PUCKIPUPPY's product wins - its delivery journey loses buyers. 11% of 500 reviews are 1-star; ~68% of those cite shipping damage, assembly, app issues, or support" - a specific structural post-purchase gap, not generic 'low awareness'. Slide 7 gives SMART objectives: "O1 (primary): 90 attributed orders via READY150 code + test-ride QR at ~$950 blended AOV" / "O3: cut damage/support-driven 1-star share from ~68% of negatives to under 50%" and Slide 8 defines P1/P2 segments with evidence cites.

research.evidence: Slide 9: "keyword-coded analysis of 500 public Judge.me reviews incl. 1-star deep-dive [R1][R2]; digital shelf/price audit of 6 sources [R4][R6]" - two completed no-survey primary methods with n and dates (2026-11-08), results summarized, and Slide 10 shows textbook finding->decision traceability ("68% of 1-stars = damage/assembly/support [R1] -> Arrive Ready unboxing + setup concierge"). Auto-capped at 10: no survey (n>=30) or interviews were fielded, and check.json counts only 2 findings cited on strategy slides.
research.fix: Field even a small survey or 3+ interviews (e.g., at the planned TX test-ride pop-ups) before the window to unlock 11-15; the finding->decision slide is already exemplary, so real primary data would carry the category.

strategy.evidence: Slide 11: "Positioning: 'the ebike that arrives ready' - own the delivery-experience gap no competitor claims [R1][R6]" with proof->protection->pathway message house, plus a control-group test design on Slide 12 ("control group gets the QR offer with no event, isolating event lift") and a live trust dashboard on Slide 13/14. The ownable element (operational delivery-experience ownership + measurable review-mix fix) is real, though the underlying tactics - inserts, creators, paid social - remain copyable.
strategy.fix: Sharpen the defensibility: tie the damage-claim promise to a contractual/logistics commitment (e.g., carrier-level packaging spec or white-glove freight partner) so 'arrives ready' is an operational moat, not just messaging; state why a competitor copying the insert can't copy the resolution SLA.

activities.evidence: Slide 16: "Wk1: Arrive Ready inserts live; trust badges above fold; test-ride bookings open; press outreach. / Wk2-4: 6 test-ride pop-ups + 8 Dog Pack creator posts; paid social/search live" and program slides name segment, weeks and owner (Slide 12: "Segment P1; weeks 1-6; owner Nino (field). Target: 400 rides, 15% quote rate"). Weakness: the week-by-week schedule does not restate segment/channel/objective per activity, and Slide 14 merges two distinct programs (Dog Pack + Ready Ledger) onto one slide.
activities.fix: Split Slide 14 into two program slides and annotate each week-block on Slide 16 with its segment/channel/objective tags so the alignment is visible on the schedule itself.

budget.evidence: Slide 17: "Total $21,000: media $8,000 [A4]; creators 8 x $800 [A6]; events 8 x $300 [A7]" - lines sum correctly (8,000+6,400+2,400+1,200+400+2,600=21,000), every line cites an assumption ID, funnel math "1.2M x 1.5% x 0.6% = ~108 orders x $950 = $102.6K" yields profit-based "ROI ~56%" and the honest conservative case "~43 orders -> -$7K, offset by 800 captures (~$12K list value)" is on-slide. Deductions: breakeven is stated as "~66 orders" but check.json computes 69; the ~$12K email-list valuation is a soft, uncited number; and the conservative ROI is still -37% (check.json W_FINANCE warning).
budget.fix: Correct breakeven to ~69 orders, cite a benchmark for email-list value (or reframe as 'asset created, valued at $X per industry CPL'), and state the post-mitigation conservative ROI explicitly instead of leaving the reader to net -$7K against +$12K.

impact.evidence: Slide 18: "O1: attributed orders - Shopify code + UTM report, weekly; target 90. / O2: test rides (event tally) + email captures (Klaviyo) - target 400/800. / O3: 1-star review share recount - re-crawl Judge.me corpus bi-weekly, same keyword method [R1]" plus leading/lagging indicators and off-track triggers. All KPIs carry targets, tools and cadence. Weaknesses: ride/capture KPIs have only "0 (new program)" baselines (deck.json kpis), there is no brand-lift or awareness KPI despite awareness being an O2-adjacent goal, and O3's "68% of negatives" vs "68% of 1-stars" wording wobbles between slides 4 and 7.
impact.fix: Unify O3 wording ('68% of 1-star reviews'), and add one awareness/consideration metric (e.g., branded-search lift or aided-recall survey of test-ride participants) so the campaign's top-of-funnel claim is measured, not assumed.

organization.evidence: Slide 3 TOC follows official IMCP order and slides run Overview -> Product/Company -> Objectives -> Target Market -> Research -> Strategy -> Budget -> Impact -> Bibliography. Deductions: Slide 14 packs two programs ("Arrive Ready Dog Pack" AND "Ready Ledger") onto one slide, and Slide 11 contains a formatting artifact: "[G1-G4]. - objective O1" - stray text that would look unpolished on the rendered slide.
organization.fix: Remove the stray '- objective O1' artifact on Slide 11 and give Ready Ledger its own slide (or fold it cleanly into the strategy slide) to restore one-idea-per-slide.

effectiveness.evidence: Slide 4 opens with an explicit thesis: "PUCKIPUPPY's product wins - its delivery journey loses buyers" and Slide 19 closes on the matching mission metric: "'X orders arrived ready, 0 unresolved damage claims' - the number we print on the trust dashboard". The proof->protection->pathway through-line (Slide 11) runs unbroken through every program slide.

delivery.evidence: check.json confirms talk-track notes on all 16 body slides, and they contain real interactive direction: Slide 4 "Open with the stat: 1 in 9 reviews is 1-star", Slide 5 "Pass around the photo", Slide 12 "judges can ride it" (product-as-demo), Slide 14 includes a control-group design, and Slide 15 directs "Show real product photography in every asset". Planned props are concrete (ride report cards, unboxing insert, QR offer).

design.evidence: All 16 body slides carry visuals (check.json body_slides_with_visual=16) and real product photography anchors slides 1, 4, 5, 8. But several 'mockups' are mislabeled: Slide 12 "Test-ride event mockup" and Slide 13 "Unboxing insert + email mockup" are just reused Labrador Pro photos (labrador_3.jpg / labrador_4.jpg), and photos/labrador_2.jpg is reused on slides 4, 11 and 15. The visuals/s06-s18 PNGs exist for 7 slides but program/creative slides rely on stock-like product shots rather than actual mockups.
design.fix: Produce at least simple rendered mockups for the test-ride card, unboxing insert, email, and trust dashboard (even wireframe-level) instead of reusing product photos, and stop repeating the same 4 photos across 10+ slides.

overall.evidence: The deck reads as a complete, professional client pitch: cited thesis, real coded review data, honest budget with conservative case, measurement triggers, and a bibliography. Residual polish gaps: meta.date reads "April 2027 (ICDC - confirm)" (an unconfirmed hedge in the deck metadata), assurances_signed is false, Slide 2/title slide still shows only campaign info with no school/address/participants/date, and Slide 11 has the stray '- objective O1' artifact.
